analysis:
## Technical analysis

### Gate 3 triple-clearance — the defining framework event

NVDA closed $200.39 on 2026-07-31, up $6.70 / +3.46% from $193.69. All three Gate 3 conditions simultaneously met on a closing basis for the first time since Gate 3 was activated July 27:

| Condition | July 30 | July 31 | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| NVDA > $200 | $193.69 (−$6.31) | $200.39 (+$0.39) | ✅ CLEARED |
| SPX > 7,460 | 7,437.63 (−22.37) | 7,505.66 (+45.66) | ✅ CLEARED |
| VIX < 17 | 17.09 (+0.09) | 16.21 (−0.79) | ✅ CLEARED |

### Trend and momentum

NVDA has re-established all key technical levels over two sessions: 200-DMA ($192.72) reclaimed July 30, $200 Gate 3 threshold cleared July 31. RSI estimated 52–55, recovering from oversold ~35 (July 29 trough) to neutral-to-bullish. The trend has shifted from step-aside/bearish-short-term (July 27–30) to recovering bullish (July 31+).

### The Amazon AWS trigger

AWS +36.7% ($42.2B revenue, 18-quarter high growth rate) is the most direct NVDA demand signal possible: AWS growth comes from AI inference and training workloads running on NVDA H100/Blackwell GPUs. Combined with Microsoft Azure +43% from the prior session, the two largest public cloud providers are simultaneously at their fastest AI-driven growth rates in years. NVDA's data center revenue is directly downstream of this demand.

### Volume — above average; confirms institutional buying

Estimated ~250M shares, above the 220M on July 30 and above the 180M baseline. Amazon AWS catalyst drove pre-market institutional positioning before the opening bell, creating above-average volume. Volume on the Gate 3 clearance day being above average is the confirming signal — not a low-conviction drift through $200 but a demand-driven break.

### Resistance-to-support conversion at $200

$200 served as resistance for 6 consecutive closes (July 25–30). Today's close above $200 converts it to support. The first test of $200 as support is Monday, August 3. If NVDA gaps down below $200 due to META overhang and fails to recover by the close, Gate 3 re-activates. If it holds, the resistance-to-support conversion is confirmed.

### Strongest support — $200 (triple-duty)

The $200 level has the most concentrated institutional attention in the NVDA framework: (1) Gate 3 price threshold — hard stop for framework traders; (2) approximate 50-DMA location; (3) highest single-strike options OI in August expiry chain. Three separate constituencies defend this level: framework rule-followers, technicals-based MA traders, and options market makers managing gamma exposure.

### Strongest resistance — $212 (pre-Gate-3 ceiling)

The $212 level is where NVDA traded in the July 22–25 window before Gate 3 was activated. Prior holders who bought in the $200–$212 zone before the July 22 selloff are now 'made whole' at various levels through that range, creating supply. A clean close above $212 signals the supply has been absorbed and the recovery is trending toward 52-week high territory.

### What invalidates the bull read

A close below $200 (Gate 3 price condition) re-activates the step-aside — immediately and regardless of SPX or VIX levels. The thin +$0.39 buffer makes this the primary near-term risk. Secondary invalidation: a close below $192.72 (200-DMA) with the step-aside already active re-confirms the July 29 structural breakdown thesis and signals the recovery from $190.27 was a bear market bounce.
